note: Each entry is a defect found by reading a real generated document. It fails now and passes when the defect is actually fixed. Text is never matched exactly — a generated document never repeats word for word.

cv.why: Applying to a Bitcoin company with the crypto work deleted. All three engagements live under an umbrella practice, so the writer collapsed them away and the only trace was the word 'crypto' in a list.
Morgan Stanley and Wells Fargo dropped entirely from a finance application — the two employer names a screener recognises on sight.
Five talks on crypto UX and a co-created blockchain workshop could not reach any CV, because no Speaking section existed in the registry.
The summary claimed 'designing and launching customer-facing digital products'. The record holds advisory work, a UX practice and QA strategy — no instance of it. Lifted from the ad to cover a gap.
The school was overwritten from a LinkedIn export after being corrected by hand more than once.
Four years of fintech and call-centre AI automation is the most relevant thing in the record for an AI-first employer.

cover.why: A letter read as marketing copy with no 'I' in it: 'participating in the ground-up launch of Airbank demonstrated that...'
Slogans dropped in as paragraph-enders: 'Friction kills adoption.', 'Execution speed matters.', 'It works. So I stay hands-on.'
A letter that never names who it is written to reads exactly like one that was written to nobody.
The employer's own copy returned to sender. Their phrasing understood, never repeated.
Crypto reduced to a one-line afterthought in a letter to a Bitcoin company.
